 Dated this the 13th day of September, 2024

Order
This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, challenging Annexure-A6 order in CMP.No.261/2024 dated 31.07.2024 on the files of Fast Track Special Judge, Haripad,
in S.C.No.898/2023 on the files of Fast Track Special Judge, Kunnamkulam arose out of Crime No.173/2023 of Vadakkekad Police Station.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor in detail.
Perused the relevant documents, including Annexure-A6 order.

3. In this matter the prosecution case is that the accused 2024:KER:70325 herein, who is a family member of the husband of the defacto complainant, reached the residential house of the defacto complainant where she has been residing along with her husband and 3 children on 22.02.2023 as part of casual visit.
After having waited for a while, while the defacto complainant was nurturing her child, he requested water to drink.
When the same was provided, after drinking water, he caught hold of her hand and put her on the bed and subjected to forcible sexual intercourse despite her resistance.
This is the base on which prosecution alleges commission of offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. In this matter, evidence recorded.
Thereafter the accused was given opportunity to adduce defence evidence.

During defence evidence, the petitioner produced his mobile phone before the trial court along with a petition (CMP.261/2024) with request to subject the same to forensic examination to retrieve the messages therein and the contention raised by the petitioner is that the petitioner and the defacto complainant though affectionately acquainted with each other no act of rape/sexual assault was committed by the petitioner.
Rather they were friends and the petitioner was falsely implicated to wreak vengeance of the defacto complainant's brother and 2024:KER:70325 husband as they belong to rival political groups.
The learned Special Judge dismissed the application in consideration of the prayer raised and the objection thereof.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner since there was companionship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant, the same can be proved by retrieving the messages available in the mobile phone, and, therefore, the petition is to be allowed in the interest of justice.
According to him, the mobile phone was already produced before the trial court, but the trial court not inclined to accept the same also.

sentences.text:
The learned Public Prosecutor would submit that now the attempt of the petitioner is to drag the proceedings by sending his mobile phone for forensic examination with a view to stall the trial,
which is at the fag end.
It is also submitted that the petitioner, in fact, destroyed all messages from his mobile phone and now he wants to retrieve the same through a Government agency, as part of the defence.

On perusal of the order in paragraph 6, the learned Special Judge observed that the mobile phone as well as the SIM card produced before the court after deleting the message and now the attempt of the petitioner to retrieve the message from 2024:KER:70325 his mobile phone would be an attempt to stall the trial and therefore the same could not be allowed.
6.

On perusal of the matter in issue, the contention raised by the petitioner is that the petitioner and the defacto complainant though affectionately acquainted with each other no act of rape/sexual assault was committed by the petitioner.
Rather they were friends and the petitioner was falsely implicated to wreak vengeance of the defacto complainant's brother and husband as they belong to rival political groups.
This contention would show that the petitioner has no case that the sexual relationship was consensual.
In such contingency, the messages in the mobile phone have no much significance in this matter.

That apart, the petitioner would have taken measures independently either to keep the messages or to retrieve the same before producing the mobile phone before the court, if he had an intention to prove anything in support of the defence case.

After deleting the messages, now his attempt to get the messages retrieved from the forensic laboratory by sending his mobile phone and SIM card, can only be held as a dilatory tactics to stall the trial.
That apart, the authenticity of the messages also is a matter of proof in so far as 2024:KER:70325 the same alleged to be sent by the defacto complainant.
Therefore, this petition must fail.
7. In the above circumstances, this Crl.M.C stands dismissed.

8. However, it is made clear that the accused is at liberty to tender the mobile phone and SIM card,
as part of evidence by resorting the procedure known to law, as part of defence evidence.
Registry shall forward a copy of this order to the jurisdictional court for information and further steps.

Sd/-
